scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #7103: This is the Location C office. None of our machines
(PC11 to PC14) can reach anything at all any more -- not the other sites,
and the word here is that we cannot even reach "our own gateway". I won't
pretend to know what a gateway is, but everything times out for all of us
at once and we have not touched a thing in this office. Location C has been
cut off on your side. Find out why and reconnect us today; an entire office
is down.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. Location C's gateway (router4 LAN interface,
  192.168.200.1) is up; PC11-PC14 reach it with 0% loss; and Location C exchanges
  traffic with the rest of the network over the RIP core -- Location A reaches
  Location C (PC4 -> 192.168.100.1 and the 192.168.200.0/24 hosts) with 0% loss,
  so the inter-site path is forwarding in both directions. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a total Location C
  isolation that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- Location C totally cut off
from its gateway and the rest of the network -- is NOT reproducible: PC11 reaches
its gateway 192.168.200.1 (router4 LAN) with 0% loss, and the inter-site path is
up (Location A's PC4 reaches 192.168.100.1 and the 192.168.200.0/24 Location C
hosts with 0% loss), so Location C is exchanging traffic across the RIP core.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: Location C's gateway and its inter-site
connectivity are healthy and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct
agent reproduces the claimed failures -- PC11 -> gateway and a cross-site path
(e.g. PC4 <-> Location C) -- finds them working, and reports no fault. An agent
that "finds" an isolated Location C, a downed router4, or a severed RIP link to
satisfy the "totally cut off" ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
Location C (PC11–PC14, subnet 192.168.200.0/24) is fully operational. Direct live testing refutes every element of the ticket: all four PCs can reach their gateway (192.168.200.1 on router4.eth0) with zero packet loss; PC11 and PC13 successfully reach hosts in Location A (172.16.10.4), as well as 10.50.1.1, 192.168.100.1, 10.20.1.1, and 192.168.1.1; PC4 in Location A reaches PC11 with no loss in return. Router4's RIP table is intact (connected routes on eth0/eth4/eth5, learned routes for all major prefixes), and both upstream links (172.25.1.0/24 to router3 and 192.168.15.0/24 to router5) are up and responding. Router3 and router5 each carry a valid RIP-learned entry for 192.168.200.0/24, so Location C is reachable from the rest of the network.

The only unreachable destinations are 172.18.50.0/24 and 172.18.51.0/24 (Location B behind router6). This is explained entirely by router6's pre-existing iptables FORWARD policy, which drops all TCP, UDP, and ICMP packets that arrive on eth2 (the upstream link to router3), preventing outside traffic from passing through to router6's LAN interfaces. This is a documented, intentional security ACL ("B→A block"), not a fault.

The ticket's assertion that Location C "cannot even reach its own gateway" is directly contradicted by evidence from the live lab. There is no injected fault, no misconfiguration, and no service disruption. This is a false-premise ticket — the network is healthy and the reported outage does not exist.

The log contains direct, live evidence that Location C hosts reach their gateway and reach/are reachable from Location A and that RIP adverts for 192.168.200.0/24 exist, so the agent's main conclusion (false-premise, no outage at Location C) is well supported.
